Let's simplify the expression by factoring both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)({x}^{3}+1)}{{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{(x-1)(x+1)({x}^{2}-x+1)}{(x-1)(x+1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(x-1)(x+1)}({x}^{2}-x+1)}{\cancel{(x-1)(x+1)}} \\  & ={x}^{2}-x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the denominator is never zero, we conclude that this function has no vertical asymptotes. A plot of the function is below. Note that it is not defined at $x=\pm 1.$
